item.title: Reducing contaminants from dairy-farm laneways
item.description: Dairy farm laneways adjacent to drains pose a risk as a potential source of contaminants to water. Laneways represent locations with large amounts of effluent loading. Furthermore, cow movement across a laneway of compacted gravels is likely to mobilise fine sediment, increasing the possibility of transport into waterways via runoff […]

item.title: Greater Wellington carbon neutrality underway with new native forest planting system
item.description: A new native forest planting system is helping Greater Wellington Regional Council achieve its biodiversity and climate change goals.

item.title: A whole system for native forest restoration
item.description: Native Forest Systems is a leading-edge approach to landscape-scale forest restoration. Queen Elizabeth Park and Battle Hill Farm Forest Park have collectively had tens of thousands of natives planted in them in 2019 using this new approach and we have a lot more planned for 2020 (if the COVID-19 situation allows for it).
